title: GS21 with the priced y factor on a fixed OPERATING COST, three cost-exposure types -- SIGNED ladder
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when firm exposure runs through operating leverage (convex in profitability) instead of a level sort?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-08, 21:30). gvy25 (y on production, level-compensated) and gvyc25 (y on a fixed cost, all exposures the same sign) both leave the EW market spanning 86-92% of SR_max with room +0.005 to +0.013: in GS21 every firm's loadings on x and on y run through the same operating-leverage channel, so the cross-section of loadings is one-dimensional and the market spans it. A SIGNED cost ladder breaks that: types +b / 0 / -b, so the market's net y loading is about zero and the y Sharpe sits entirely outside the market. The type remains hidden at y = 0 (same cost for every type). The known risk, from the reduced-form screen: a premium that rotates with the state is the BGN/GS state signature, which the ranks x state linear benchmark (linrank_s) absorbs; so room_s against room is the first thing to read.

CALIBRATION (low resolution, xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 150 firms, 2026-10-08 21:20): fc 0.2 with gs_bc +0.3 / 0 / -0.3 gives type premia 0.3 / 3.4 / 9.3 %/yr (convex in the exposure: the hedge type loses 3, the exposed type gains 6), SR_max 0.27-0.34 by y-tercile, mean log size 4.02 / 3.93 / 3.76. Half-width 0.4 is used here so that SR_max sits nearer vyg25/bvy25 (0.5-0.6): the -0.4 point alone gave 13.2 %/yr at this resolution.

CHECKS. E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 on the calibration economy; the solver at NY = 1 and gs_fc = 0 is gs_solve_reg.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids read from the Quest solve logs by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-08, before the run). Market share of SR_max below 50% (from 86-92%); room above +0.03; the decisive number is room_s: if room_s is close to room the premium is rank-nonlinear given the state and a fair gap of +0.005 to +0.015 follows; if room_s is well below room the economy has the state signature and the fair gap with linrank_s is about zero. FALSIFIED as 'a signed ladder makes the KP mechanism work in GS21' if the fair gap is below +0.005 or positive in fewer than 7 of 10 seeds.

changes: gs_fc 0.2: a fixed operating cost per unit capital (0 in gvy25 and gsbase)
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.4, 0.0, -0.4]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35
the -0.4 type IS gvyc25's third solve (identical parameters; the content-addressed producer reported it cached), so sol_gvyc25c is reused as gx7 reused sol_g28

method.gs_vy_exposure: cost-side: fixed cost gs_fc * exp(gs_bc y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
